note: World catalogue (spec docs/specs/2026-11-09-global-spots.md); not in the app. Spot list = every Surfnerd Indonesia page (238, 13 provinces) plus every Surf-Forecast.com and Wannasurf Indonesia break page. Positions are Surfnerd guide map pins rounded to 3 dp; seaward = Surfnerd "Faces X" in degrees. Facts quote Surfnerd, Surf-Forecast.com and Wannasurf with attribution; pages were matched by name within 6 km (a few same-name pages farther apart were paired by hand, with the distance kept in notes). Where Surfnerd's facing lies outside its own swell-exposure range the notes say so. Time zones follow the province: WIB Asia/Jakarta (Sumatra, Java), WITA Asia/Makassar (Bali, Nusa Tenggara), WIT Asia/Jayapura (North Maluku); each matches the Surfnerd page time zone. nearestSources: great-circle km to IOC sea-level stations (liveness from each station's public data table on 2026-11-09) and IEM ID__ASOS airport METARs. No public live wave buoy exists for these coasts in NDBC activestations (only RAMA moorings and DART tsunami buoys) and none was found from BMKG, so no wave buoy is listed.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Cobras is a swell-magnet left at the southern end of the island, breaking over live coral. On the right swell it lines up a long, superlative barrel, and it becomes a go-to spot when the swell is small elsewhere. Across the deep channel sits a separate right called Warrens, so don't confuse the two when you're picking your peak.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Airport Rights is a right-hand reef break that peels beside the airport runway, and it counts as one of Bali's premier waves. On its day it throws flawless, deep barrels that spin the length of the reef triangle. It's a fairly fickle setup that breaks over dead coral and can slam shut through sections, so the truly special days don't come around all that often by Indonesian standards.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Airport Rights in Bali (Kuta) is an exposed reef break that only works when conditions are just right. May-Oct (Dry Season) is the best time of year for waves. Watch out for rips and rocks.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Balian is a rivermouth rock shelf peak that reliably pulls in swell, throwing the bulk of its size and power into a long left. It often runs noticeably bigger than the other west coast beaches nearby. The peaks are shifty and steep, and they can arrive unannounced, sweeping up the lineup.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Balian in Bali (West Coast) is an exposed reef break that has consistent surf. May-Oct (Dry Season) is the favoured time of year for waves. Offshore winds blow from the northeast. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the ideal swell direction is from the southwest. Reef breaks provide lefts and rights. Good surf at all stages of the tide. When the surf is up, it can get quite busy in the water. Watch out for rocks.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Canggu is a reef break just north of Kuta on Bali's black-sand coast, throwing up both lefts and rights over a mix of uneven reef and sand. The black sand moves around the reef and the sets shift with it, so the peaks are rarely in quite the same place twice. It usually runs a touch bigger than Kuta, and there are more peaks scattered down the beach towards Pererenan.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Canggu in Bali (West Coast) is an exposed reef break that has reliable surf. May-Oct (Dry Season) is the best time of year for waves. When the surf is up, it can get quite busy in the water. Hazards include rips and rocks.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Dreamland is a peak on Bali's Bukit peninsula, throwing a short left wall and a shouldering right off the takeoff over a sandy reef platform that sits good and deep. Once a quiet beach, it now lies beneath a sprawl of large-scale hotel, golf course and condo development running across the Bukit from Balangan to Bingin, so expect a busy, well-serviced tourist scene rather than a soulful hideaway.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Dreamland in Bali (The Bukit) is a quite exposed beach and reef break that has fairly consistent surf. May-Oct (Dry Season) is the favoured time of year for waves. Offshore winds blow from the east. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the ideal swell angle is from the southwest. Both left and right reef breaks. Best around low tide. It's sometimes crowded here. Submerged rocks are a hazard.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Green Ball is a swell-magnet right that breaks over live coral, tucked at the bottom of a long, strenuous cliff path and a fair hike from anywhere. It has a lot in common with nearby Nyang Nyang, including heavy exposure to the trade winds. When the wind stays off it, the right sucks and spins fast off the reef, then walls up nicely before pitting on the last section of reef before the channel.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Green Ball in Bali (The Bukit) is an exposed reef break that has fairly consistent surf. Nov-April (Wet Season) provides favoured time of year for waves. Offshore winds are from the north. Groundswells are more common than windswells and the best swell direction is from the south southwest. There are left and right breaking reefs. Best around mid tide. It's sometimes crowded here. Watch out for rips and rocks.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Hyatt Reef is a right-hand reef break sitting off the upmarket hotel strip, where tourists mess about on the calm lagoon while surfers make the long boat trek out to the barrier reef. The energetic righthanders rumble off the furthest point, split into two sections by a big hole in the reef. The outer peaks are hap-hazard and rip-torn, sharing something with Nusa Dua but breaking even hollower.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Sanur - Grand Hyatt in Bali (Sanur) is a reasonably exposed reef break that only works once in a while. Nov-April (Wet Season) provides optimum time of year for waves. Offshore winds are from the west northwest. Groundswells are more common than windswells and the ideal swell angle is from the south. A right hand reef. Best around mid tide when the tide is rising. A popular wave that can get growded. Beware of rocks/rips.

From the cliffs it looks picture perfect, but the wave earns its name: at some point it becomes impossibly fast. The reef breaks into roughly three sections separated by straight stretches of reef, so getting caught behind the curtain is part of the deal.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Jimbaran is a sandy beachbreak on Bali's west side that spends most of the year as a gentle, crumbling shorebreak. It's the escape plan when Kuta is maxed out, and a friendly place for kids to get to grips with waves without the fear or the crowds. Longboards suit it well, and it's a good spot to learn SUP.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Jimbaran Beach in Kuta - Bali is a sheltered beach break that only works when conditions are just right. May-Oct (Dry Season) is the favoured time of year for waves. Works best in offshore winds from the east southeast. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the ideal swell angle is from the west. The beach break provides left and right handers. The quality of the surf isn't affected by the tide. Even when there are waves, it's not likley to be crowded. Take care of the strong rips here.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Keramas is a right-hand reef break with a big reputation for barrels and high-performance surfing, and it now draws the pro contest scene. The wave breaks over a jagged lava reef and opens up straight from the drop, giving you a wall to work before it closes out on the inside. On its day it can barrel all the way through; other times it leaves an open face for turns and aerials, particularly on the steeper end section.

If you want a more manageable ride, there are gentler reefs nestled among the black sand beachbreak on either side.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Kuta Beach is Bali's most famous stretch of surf, a fine-grained beach break that has been introducing people to the sport since the 1930s. The tropical setting is largely buried under concrete these days, but the place still carries an aura that pulls in surfers of every level. On its day it throws up super-fast tunnels; other times it's all dribbly, knee-high corners.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Kuta Beach in Bali (Kuta) is an exposed beach break that has reliable surf. May-Oct (Dry Season) is the optimum time of year for waves. The best wind direction is from the east northeast. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the best swell direction is from the southwest. The beach breaks offer lefts and rights. Take care of locals and pollution.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Kuta Reef is the original Bali reefbreak, a left that sits a good 700 metres offshore and breaks over dead coral. It waits for enough swell to swing around the projecting runway before lighting up a couple of sections of reef. The main reef is the pick: a drop, stall, barrel and slash left that turns ledgy once the faces push into the 8-10ft range.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Kuta Reef in Bali (Kuta) is an exposed reef break that is usually a safe bet. May-Oct (Dry Season) is the optimum time of year for waves. Offshore winds blow from the east northeast. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the ideal swell angle is from the southwest. A left hand reef break. It's often crowded here. Hazards include rips and pollution.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Lacerations is a hardcore right-hander that hands out wide open, high-quality tube time over sharp, shallow live coral. The entry is a pitching air-drop straight off the peak into a clean barrel section, followed by a second sucky bowl as the wave runs toward the channel, which is marked by the floating mooring lines scattered across the bay. It isn't easy, it isn't long, and it isn't empty, and it's a clear step up in difficulty from neighbouring Shipwrecks and Playgrounds.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Lacerations (Nusa Lembongan) in Bali (Nusa Lembongan) is a sheltered reef break that has inconsistent surf. May-Oct (Dry Season) is the optimum time of year for waves. Works best in offshore winds from the east southeast. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the best swell direction is from the southwest. A right hand reef break. Best around high tide. A popular wave that can get growded. Beware of rips, rocks, man-made danger (buoys etc...) and locals.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Padang Padang is the benchmark Bali barrel machine, a short left reef tucked into the peninsula below the cliffs and home to some of the best lefts on the planet. The ride is only around 50 metres, but it packs plenty in: a pitching lip take-off sets up a perfectly cylindrical wall that tempts experts to stand on the tail and see how deep they can push it. As the barrel draws more water off the shallow dead coral, the intensity ramps up and forces a flat-out speed run to reach the exit before the wave runs out of water.

When it's working here, it can get crowded. Rocks are a hazard.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Playgrounds is the most user-friendly spot on Lembongan, a reef break tucked below cliffs that shelter it from the southeast trade winds. It sits closer to shore than the breaks nearby, so the paddle out is easier, and the deeper water gives you more wall to work rather than the flat-out barrels next door. Both lefts and rights come through, but the lefts are the pick, offering a few lip-bashing sections along a tapered wall.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Playgrounds (Nusa Lembongan) in Bali (Nusa Lembongan) is a sheltered reef break that has reliable surf. May-Oct (Dry Season) is the best time of year for waves. Works best in offshore winds from the east southeast with some shelter here from southeast winds. Clean groundswells prevail and the ideal swell direction is from the southwest. There are left and right breaking reefs. Best around mid tide. Sometimes crowded. Take care of urchins, rocks and rips.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Serangan, also known as Turtle Island, is an east-facing reef that comes alive in the wet season and has something for just about everyone. Lefts and rights peak up and pitch along a curving coral arc, ranging from softer shoulders to hollow, pitching sections. It breaks over dead coral and sits right beside a massive rock jetty, which is a strange thing to surf next to in Bali, though it has little effect on the waves as they hit the nicely oriented reef.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Serangan (Bali) in Sanur - Bali is a fairly exposed reef break that has consistent surf. Nov-April (Wet Season) provides favoured time of year for waves. Offshore winds are from the northwest and there is no shelter here from cross shore breezes. Groundswells are more common than windswells and the optimum swell angle is from the south southeast. No reef break here. Likely to be crowded if working. Overcrowding can even make surfing hazardous.

guideSummary.surfnerd: N'Dana is a super-fun left that peels off the northwest point, breaking over a reef of dead coral. The main wall bends through several shifting sections, and there's more to explore around the headland, where a handful of fun peaks and another left run along the exposed west coast. It works year round and picks up most swells, so there's usually something on offer.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Ndana in Timor is an exposed reef break that has very consistent waves. May-Oct (Dry Season) is the favoured time of year for waves. Works best in offshore winds from the northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the optimum swell angle is from the southwest. A choice of left and right reefs. It very rarely gets crowded here. Rocks are a hazard.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Ndao is a fast, steep reef break sitting about 15 km off the southwestern tip of Timor, near Rote, the southernmost island in Indonesia. It's an outer island where the people are very different from their neighbours and speak their own language. The western reef tip catches good swell exposure, and the wave breaks over dead coral with steep drops that run into racy walls.

It very rarely gets crowded here. Rocks are a hazard.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Nihiwatu is a left-hand reef break on Sumba, often called "Occy's Lefts", peeling over an uneven reef. It's one of Indonesia's more unusual setups: the deluxe resort fronting the wave claims exclusive use for its guests, capping the lineup at eight surfers to avoid the usual surf-slum scene and to channel more benefit to local communities through the Sumba Foundation. Staying in the resort's cottages runs around $236 to $454 per day.

guideSummary.surfnerd: G-Land is a long left-hand reef break over dead coral, made up of several distinct sections that peel down the point. Furthest out is Kong's, the messiest part of the reef, peaking up haphazardly and prone to shifting; west swell makes it slab and barrel, while south swell walls up and offers more shoulder. Money Trees is the heart of the setup, throwing what look like perfect barrels for 200 to 300 metres.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Belongas is an isolated left-hand reef that peels over live coral, with a racy lip line and a few tuck sections to aim for. It sits on a large, apparently sharky bay, and there's more on offer than just the left: a fun, often fast righthander breaks across the water when there's plenty of south swell and wet-season northwesterlies, and deeper inside the bay the reef cut at Meang can serve up slow lefts and rights in windless or northerly conditions.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Belongas in South Lombok is a sheltered reef break that has reasonably consistent surf. Nov-April (Wet Season) provides favoured time of year for waves. The best wind direction is from the north northwest. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the ideal swell angle is from the south southwest. There are left and right breaking reefs. Good surf at all stages of the tide. Relatively few surfers here, even on good days. Watch out for sharks,.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Benete is a classic left-hand point that reels over live coral beneath cliffs, tucked deep inside a well-protected bay. A major containership terminal and port sits only 5 km down the coast, which tells you plenty about how sheltered this stretch really is. The wave runs top to bottom from the peak all the way to a final section that closes out, and there is nowhere to go if you get caught inside by the shifting peak.

Clean groundswells prevail and the ideal swell angle is from the southwest. There is a left breaking reef. Best around high tide when the tide is rising. Sometimes crowded. Beware of urchins, rocks, pollution and sharks.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Gili Air is a right-hand reef that peels over live coral off the southeast tip of the island. It rarely comes together: the spot sits well protected from swell and goes dead onshore whenever the southeast trades blow, so a clean session here is a rare score. When it does turn on, it throws short, sharp barrels down the southeast tip, with straighter lefts on the other side and a few fickle corners across on neighbouring Gili Meno.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Inside Ekas is a generously covered reef peak marooned deep inside a bay and estuary, breaking over live coral. The peak splits into two distinct waves: the shorter rights are sucky and swift, feathering up nicely and opening up now and then, while the longer lefts wall and roll predictably and invite big hits.

It can pick up quickly without warning, sometimes bringing cool, deep water up from the channel.

It sits further down the reef from the neighbouring wedge, where the reef curves into a proper channel. That channel is what sets it apart: the wave is more likely to hold up and spin off makeable barrels rather than ending abruptly.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Greenbush is a left-hand reef break that peels over live coral. On its day it throws an extremely hollow, uber-tube: a vertical drop, a stall to set up the barrel, then hard on the gas as the wave coils and accelerates over ever-shallower reef. It can spit you out into the channel or slam the door shut, but you are safer staying in the barrel than trying to straighten out.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Green Bush in Mentawi Islands is an exposed reef break that is often working. May-Oct (Dry Season) is the best time of year for waves. Offshore winds are from the east northeast with some shelter here from north winds. Groundswells are more common than windswells and the ideal swell direction is from the southwest. There is no reef break. Good surf at all stages of the tide. An uncrowded break, even when it is working. Watch out for rocks.

How much swell is running decides whether those three connect into one long wall and whether there's room to fit turns in.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Macaronis is a machine-like left that many rate as the funnest wave in the Mentawais. It peels along a coral platform that curves into a deep bay, breaking over live coral at a fairly predictable speed. Rides open with a perfect pipe section and often finish on a ruler-edge quarter-pipe wall, so there's room for barrels, lip hits, and airs on a single wave.

Offshore winds blow from the northeast. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the ideal swell angle is from the southwest. A reef breaks left. Good surf at all stages of the tide. A fairly popluar wave that can sometimes get crowded Rocks are a hazard.

That position makes it approachable: intermediates get a chance to work the consistent walls without taking on something beyond them, while still riding something with a bit of juice. Big drops can be had across a couple of sections of reef, and the inside zippers can offer a tube ride.

guideSummary.surfnerd: No-Kandui is one of the most demanding lefts in the Mentawai, a cylindrical barrel that peels along a fringing reef down the west coast of Karangmajat Island. The line-up is featureless, so working out exactly where to sit is half the battle, and the wave rarely backs off enough to let you turn. This is a tube from start to finish, spinning down a straight 500 m stretch of reef with cavernous sections the whole way.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Rag's Right is a fast, heavy right-hand reef in the Mentawais and one of the gnarliest waves in the area. It breaks over live coral and kicks off with a beyond-vertical, no-mistakes take-off into undulating, sometimes square barrels that run down a featureless reef. The tube time is long and the coral is sharp and barely covered, so it demands constant speed and readjustment behind the curtain, and coral heads can appear at the exit.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Rags Right in Sumatra (Mentawi Islands) is an exposed reef break that has consistent surf. May-Oct (Dry Season) is the favoured time of year for waves. Ideal winds are from the east. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the ideal swell direction is from the southwest. There is a right breaking reef. Unlikely to be too crowded, even when the surf is up. Take care of rocks in the line up.

Breaking over live coral, it's a gun-barrel, straight-shooting righthander, a super-sprint where you have to stay ahead of the foamball and keep pace with constantly peeling sections. It isn't always perfect and will shut down unmakeable sections, but when everything aligns it's world-class.
